dedupe_keys.name: peering strategic game models for interdependent isps in content centric internet

description: This 2013 paper proposes peering for content exchange between interdependent internet service providers in a content-centric Internet, where ISPs cache content in their own routers and must decide how far to share it. It models four peering strategic games that represent relationships from egoism to altruism, with ISPs acting either as individual profit-makers or as a profit coalition, and reports simulation results for the price of anarchy and communication cost. The conclusion is that ISPs should balance intradomain content demand against interdomain peering relations to minimise delivery cost. Producer: researchers at Beijing Jiaotong University and Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications, published in The Scientific World Journal. Coverage: abstract network models, not a specific country. Access: full text on PubMed Central. Licence and cost: free; the article states a Creative Commons Attribution licence. Caveats: no code or dataset is released on the page, the simulations use synthetic topologies, and the setting is a proposed future architecture. Simulation uses: the game formulations can be reused to study peering and interconnection decisions of networks at exchange points. Related record: the global evidence on the cost of peering at IXPs (case_study-cost-of-peering-ixp-versus-ip-transit-global-evidence).
